extracted.intended_audience: scientists, academicians, and scientific administrators (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: A Nature issue page containing book review/commentary and reports from scientific assemblies (International Association of Academies, British Association), including procedural recommendations for geodetic/meteorological work and a methodological description for cranial comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and organisation of meteorological stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the distribution of meteorological stations over the globe shows that stations in the far north and on islands in the various oceans are of special importance; Governments concerned should take steps for securing continuance of observations where they already exist; for modifying their form, if necessary, to bring them into conformity with meteorological usage; for establishing stations where they do not yet exist; and for placing the observations at the service of science by suitable publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As regards the far north, observations are desired from two or three stations, at least, in the north of Siberia and of the Continent of America respectively. A specific suggested list of islands/regions to be covered is provided (Greenland, Fseroe Islands, Azores, Madeira, Canaries, Cape Verde, Ascension, St. Helena, Falklands, Fernando Naronha, Staten Island, Fernando Po, West Indies, Bermudas, Sandwich Islands, Carolines, Guam, Bismarck Archipelago, Samoa, Fiji, New Caledonia, Tahiti, Java, Borneo, Seychelles, Maurice, Reunion, Madagascar, Zanzibar, Socotra, Chagos Archipelago, Christmas Island, Karmaluki). The recommendation emphasises government action, conformity of data-forms to meteorological usage, establishment where absent, and publication for scientific service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency for repeating precise levelling operations
rubrics_metrics.description: A report on levelling operations urged the desirability of repeating precise levellings two or three times per century in all countries, in order to determine possible changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation sets a frequency (2–3 times per century) as adequate for detecting long-term changes; it is a nationwide/international standard to be adopted by countries conducting precise levellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Baron Eötvös apparatus for gravity-anomaly studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperation of the International Geodetic Association in geological researches by means of the study of anomalies in the value of gravity was reported feasible using the apparatus of Baron Eötvös.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouragement is sought for experiments with this apparatus; practical difficulties (especially lack of funds) in organising cooperation are acknowledged. The Hungarian Government's promise of annual support for work with the apparatus is given as an example of enabling such research. Recommendation: governments should encourage and fund experiments with appropriate apparatus to enable international cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for International Union for Solar Research patronage
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Union for Solar Research successfully solicited the patronage of the association, in token whereof they were to report to it every three years, and to reserve one place on the executive committee (of three members) for a member to be nominated by the leading academy for the time being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patronage is conditional: triennial reporting to the association and guaranteed representation (one of three executive seats) nominated by the leading academy; this is a model for incorporating international research unions into academy oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence in agenda selection for international assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: It was decided by small majorities not to place on the agenda paper either the selection of an auxiliary language or the proposal for a symbolic nomenclature for machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion that contentious or potentially divisive items (auxiliary language, symbolic nomenclature) may be excluded from agendas by small-majority decisions to avoid unproductive debate; implies a criterion of practicality/consensus when setting meeting agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for quantitative cranial comparison (ophryo-tentorial metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A method of comparing skulls by drawing a line A-B from ophryon (median point across narrowest part of frontal bone) to the extra-tentorial point between the occipital ridges (the ophryo-tentorial baseline); lines e and f are perpendiculars drawn respectively from the median point of A-B and the junction of the third with the posterior fourth of the same line; A-C is drawn from ophryon to bregma and line li (perpendicular) from A-C to the most prominent point of the frontal boss; the depths (lines d, e, f) are expressed numerically as percentages of the ophryo-tentorial length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these specified anatomical landmarks and perpendiculars to quantify differences in cranial dome depth and frontal boss development; express measurements as percentages of ophryo-tentorial length to enable comparative analysis across specimens. Photographic reproduction of representative skulls aids illustration; choose suitable examples not for presumed superiority but for photographic suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key morphological criteria for human vs ape cranial differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The three great features of difference between ancient (e.g., Java/Pithecanthropus) and later (e.g., Greek) skulls are: (1) the great size of the eyebrow ridges; (2) the much greater relative height of the middle and back part of the cranial dome; (3) the much greater prominence in the Greek skull of the front part of the cranial dome — the prefrontal area or frontal 'boss'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These external cranial features correspond to internal brain convolution differences (areas specially developed in man compared with the highest apes) and should be the focus when assessing evolutionary cranial change; present comparisons with quantified measurements (see ophthalmic-tentorial method) for rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of effective scientific/popular essays and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective essays (as exemplified by the reviewed collection) should trace history and argument (e.g., man’s rebellion and destiny), render a brief general account of advance in major scientific departments 'supremely interesting', and supply a powerful imaginative motive force for reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confining attention to a central argument and illustrating it with striking examples (successes and failures of science) strengthens impact. A successful presidential/lecture address should combine historical perspective, vivid illustration, and an appeal to imagination to move public and institutional opinion toward reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for international publication and cooperation on scholarly works
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association expressed the hope that the academies which prepared a catalogue of the Leibniz MSS. would proceed to undertake and carry through a scientifically complete edition of the works of Leibniz, and that the necessary Government aid would be forthcoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards implied: produce a scientifically complete edition; cooperation among multiple national academies; secure governmental support for large editorial projects; publish and circulate results widely as part of scholarly duty.
